description_en: Bāghabhairava is the oldest and the largest temple in Kirtipur. The residents of Kirtipur worship Bāgabhairava as their favorite deity (arādhyadeva) and call him Dhũ-āju (the deity in the form a tiger). The premises of Bāghabhairava is also known as Gũde. Thus, Bāghavairava is also called Gundesthānādhipati (the lord of the place called Gunde) (see the following inscription dating 707 NS), Vyāghreśvara Bhaṭṭāraka, Vyāghrabhailava, Ajāju, and so forth. According to one of the inscriptions, he is even believed to be a form of Bhīmasena.P. Pāla(1974, 11) suggests that this tradition of worshipping a tiger as Bhairava could be an ancient form of nature worship 'prakṛti’.There is no documented evidence to date the initial construction of the Bāghabhairava Mandira. The earliest inscription related to this temple was issued in 1514 CE (635 NS), recording its renovation by a powerful elite called ‘Mahāpātra’ of Patan. In the light of this evidence, the temple must have been constructed before 1514 CE (635 NS).Ś. Śreṣṭha(VS 2057, 39) suggests that King Śivadeva could have built it during his reign.[1]However, this assumption cannot be verified without further documented evidences.Similar to other Bhairava temples in the Kathmandu Valley, Bāghabhairava Mandira stands on a rectangular platform. At first glance, it looks like a three-storey structure although it actually has four floors. This is one of the temples in the Kathmandu Valley which survived in its original architectural style (cf,Tivari1994, 130). While its first two layers of roof are tiled withjhĩgaṭībricks, the third one is covered with copper sheets and crowned with a pinnacle. A statue of Bāghabhairava is consecrated in its sanctum, facing east. The front part of the statue is wrapped with silver and its lower part is sculpted of mud.There is a shrine called Hiphaḥdyaḥ (the deity which demands blood sacrifice) in one of the façades of the temple. An aniconic stone representing the main Bāghabhairava statue of the sanctum is kept in this shrine. All the sacrificial offerings for the main statue is also offered to this aniconic stone. The ground floor of Bāghabhairava Mandira has beautiful murals. These murals are very rare examples of medieval art so far preserved in the Kathmandu Valley. There are still several weapons safeguarded on the temple’s third floor. It is strongly believed that these weapons were seized by the Gorkhali army when they attacked Kirtipur in 1757 CE. A shrine for Nāsaḥdyaḥ was built on the western side of this temple. The residents of Kirtipur believe that Nāsaḥdyaḥ should be voluntarily worshipped by offering an animal sacrifice if someone from the region organizes a singing or dancing activity.A procession as well as several other religious and cultural activities take place in this temple on every first solar day of Bhādra (siṃhasaṃkrāntiday). During this procession, a small silver statue is mounted to a chariot and taken around the city.[2]Footnotes^TheGopālarājavaṁśāvalī(1985, fol. 31) records that King Śivadeva the 3rd made Kirtipur inhabitable by constructing the water supply facilities there. He reigned from 1099-1126 CE (cf.Slusser1982, Appendix III, Table III 2).^It is not clear whether the complete statue is a metal made and its front part is wrapped in silver or it is made out of mud, and its front part is wrapped in silver.
description_ne: बाघभैरव मन्दिर कीर्तिपुरको सबैभन्दा ठुलो र पुरानो मन्दिर हो । कीर्तिपुरवासीको मुख्य आरध्यदेव भएकाले बाघभैरवप्रति कीर्तिपुरवासीमा विशिष्ट भक्ति भाव पाइन्छ । उपत्यकामा वोलीचालीको भाषामा आफ्नो वस्तीको आरध्य देवलाई ‘आजु’ भन्ने चलन छ । बाघको स्वरूपमा रहेका आरध्यदेव भएबाट यिनलाई कीर्तिपुरमा धुँआजु भन्ने गरिन्छ जुसको अर्थ बाघको स्वरूप भएका आरध्यदेव भन्ने हुन्छ । आजु भएको स्थान भएबाट यस मन्दिर परिसरलाई पनि ‘आजुथाय्’ (आजुको स्थान) भनिँदै आएको छ ।  वस्तीको मध्य भागमा अवस्थित आजुथाय् अर्थात् बाघभैरव परिसर कीर्तिपुरकै मुख्य धार्मिक एवं सांस्कृतिक केन्द्र पनि हो । यस परिसरलाई गुँदे पनि भनिन्छ । दोलखाका आरध्यदेवलाई त्यस स्थानका मालिक अर्थात् दोलखाधिपति भने जस्तै गुँदेका अधिपतिका रूपमा नेसं ७०७ को अभिलेखमा बाघभैरवलाई गुन्देस्थानाधिपति भनिएको पनि पाइएको छ ।बाघभैरव परिसरबाट प्राप्त अभिलेखहरूमा उनलाई व्याघ्रेश्वर भट्टारक, ब्याघ्रभैलव, गन्दे स्थानाधिपति, अजाजु आदि विविध नामबाट सम्बोधन गरिएको पाइन्छ । एक अभिलेखमा त उनलाई भीमसेनको अवतारका रूपमा भीमसेन भट्टारक पनि भनिएको छ । पालले भैरव मानी बाघलाई पूज्ने यस  पृथक चलनभित्र प्रकृतिलाई पूज्ने प्राचीन मानव पराम्पराको अवशेष लुकेको हुन सक्ने कुरा इ‌ंगित गरेका छन् (P. Pāla1974, 11) ।बाघभैरव मन्दिरको निर्माता एवं निर्माणमितिका सन्धर्भमा कुनै पनि अभिलेख्य प्रमाण हालसम्म पाइएको छैन । सन् १५१४ अर्थात् नेसं ६३५ मा पाटनका शक्तिशाली महापात्र जगतपालले यसको जीर्णोद्धार गरेको अभिलेख नै यस मन्दिरसंग सम्बन्धित पहिलो अभिलेख हो । यसबाट सन् १५१४ भन्दा निकै अघि देखि यो मन्दिर अस्तित्वमा थियो भनी स्वीकार्न सकिन्छ । गोपालराजवंशावलीमा राजा शिवदेव तृतीयले कीर्तिपुरमा नहर कुलो ल्याई पोखरी एवं सिँचाईको व्यवस्था मिलाई वस्न योग्य बनाएको प्रसंग छ (Gopālarājavaṁśāvalī1985, fol. 31) । शिवदेव तृतीयको अवधि सन् १०९९ देखि ११२६ सम्म हो (Slusser1982, Appendex III, Table III 2) । यसलाई आधार मानी शुक्रसागरले (Ś. ŚreṣṭhaVS 2057, 39) यिनै शिवदेवले उनको शासन अवधि बीचमा यो मन्दिर पनि निर्माण गरेको हुन सक्ने अड्कल गरेका छन् । तर कुनै ठोस ऐतिहासिक प्रमाण बिना यो कुरालाई सहजै स्वीकार्न सकिँदैन । जगतपालले सन् १५१५ मा मन्दिर जीर्णोद्धार गरेको अभिलेख पश्चात् मन्दिरमा विविध वस्तु थप्ने तथा निर्माण कार्यहरू हुँदै गएको तथ्य उल्लेखित राणाकाल सम्मका थुप्रै अभिलेखहरू मन्दिर परिसरमा पाइन्छन् ।उपत्यकाका अन्य भैरव मन्दिर जस्तै यो मन्दिर पनि वर्गाकार नभई आयताकार शैलीमा उभिएको छ । बाहिरबाट तीन तले देखिए तापनि भित्रबाट यो मन्दिर चार तले छ । हालसम्म मौलिक शैलीमा बचेका उपत्यकाका मन्दिरहरूमध्ये यो पनि एक हो (Tivari1994, 130) । दुई तलासम्म झिंगटीले छाई माथिल्लो तल्लामा भने तामाको पातले छानो ढाकिएको छ । मन्दिरको उचो भागमा पुर उठाई गजूर चढाइएको छ । मन्दिरको मुख्य प्रवेश द्वार, द्वारका सिंह र तोरणलाई तामाको पाताले मोडी सजाइएको छ । गभृगृहभित्र बाघभैरवको मूर्ति पूर्वतिर फर्काई स्थापना गरिएको छ । बाघरूपी मूर्तिको छातीदेखि पछाडिको भाग माटोबाट भनेको छ भने छातीभन्दा माथि शिरसम्मको भाग चाँढीको पाता थोकी बनाइएको छ (Repoussé) । मूर्ति, मूर्तिको आशन लगायत मूर्ति आसपासको भाग चाँदी एवं पित्तलको विविध सामाग्रीको प्रयोगले साज–सज्जा गरिएको छ । मन्दिरको मोहोडा भागमा एक देवस्थल छ जसलाई हिफःद्यः भनिन्छ । हिफःद्यःको अर्थ रगत ग्रहण गर्ने देवता (sacrificing altar) भन्ने हुन्छ । भित्रको बाघभैरव मूर्तिको ठिक बाहिर बाघभैरवकै अमूर्त स्वरूपका रूपमा यो देवस्थल बनाइएको छ ।  बाघभैरवलाई चढाइने सम्पूर्ण बलि यसै देवस्थलमा चढाइन्छ ।यस मन्दिरको भूमि तल्लाको तीनतर्फी भित्तामा भित्तेचित्रहरू छन् । उपत्यकामा निकै कम संख्यामा बचेका मध्यकालीन भित्तेचित्रहरूको सूचीमा यहाँको भित्तेचित्र पनि पर्दछ ।  मन्दिरको मोहोडा भागको तेस्रो तल्लामा विभिन्न मध्येकालीन हात–हतियारहरू टाँगिएका छन् । यी हतियारहरू कीर्तिपुर र गोरखाबीच भएको प्रथम युद्धमा कीर्तिपुरेबाट खोसिएका हुन् भन्ने बलियो विश्वास कीर्तिपुरवासीमा पाइन्छ । यसै मन्दिरको पश्चिमी भित्तामा गाभेर नासःद्यःको देवस्थल बनाइएको छ । कीर्तिपुरभित्र जुन स्थानमा बाद्यवादन, गायन वा नाच प्रशिक्षण गरिए तापनि यस नासःद्यःलाई अनिवार्य पूजी बलि चढाउनु पर्ने मान्यता यद्यपि चली आएको छ ।प्रति वर्ष सिंह संक्रान्तिका दिन (भदौ १ गते) बाघभैरवको जात्रा हुने गर्दछ । जात्रामा बाघभैरवकोे सानो चाँदीको मूर्ति खतमा राखी कीर्तिपुर नगर परिक्रमा गराइन्छ । मूल जात्रा बाहेक बाघभैरवसंग सम्बन्धित अनेक धार्मिक एवं सांस्कृतिक गतिविधिहरू रहेका छन् ।
monument_assessment: Good (very few light surface damages, renovated or repaired)

historical_events.event_description: During the reign of King Yoganarendra Malla, something was offered to Bāghabhairava. Since the part of the inscription recording of this event is rubbed off, what exactly offered remains obscure.
Bijaya Bhāva from Thāna Bāhāla and his grandsons Bhāginātha Bhāva, Dharmanātha Bhāva, Dhanadeva Bhāva, and Siddhinātha Bhāva paved the temple premises with stones.

historical_events.event_name: Offering of a Toraṇa and Other Metal Objects
historical_events.event_description: During the reign of King Prithvī Vīra Vikrama, Jamadāra Bhīma Narasiṃha Bhāvo and his other family members offered a gilttoraṇaand other brass objects to Bāghabhairava.
Ratnabahādura Śāhī offered a brasspatāḥto the temple.

During the reign of King Śrīnivāsa Malla, Viṣvasiṃha Rāutta, Rāma Rāutta, Nalasiṃha Bhāro, and Nalasiṃha Bhāvo jointly built the stone plinth in the façade of the Nāsaḥdyaḥ shrine (see the object number KIR0004-009 above).

historical_events.event_name: Thievery of the Gilt Toraṇa Offered in 1897 CE and Installation of a New One
historical_events.event_description: Since the gilttoraṇa,which was offered in 1897 CE, was stolen in around 1994 CE, the Kirtipur United Club installed a newtoraṇato its place with the financial support of Śaṅkara Maharjana.
Tulārāma and his family members renovated the temple.

historical_events.event_name: Land Grant and Offering of Silver Jewellery
historical_events.event_description: Kvāthanāyaka Duṇḍirāja Bhāro and his wife Cikuṭi offered some silver jewelry. They also granted some plots of land from four different areas to aguṭhīto maintain lighting the lamp which refer to asmahādīpa(great light) in the inscription.
Maṅgala Dāsa and Putali Nāni from Kutujvaḥ Ṭola, Kirtipur wrapped in brass the lions, flanking the main entrance of the temple.

historical_events.event_name: Inscription Issued by King Rājyaprakāśa of Kāntipura (Kathmandu)
historical_events.event_description: The inscription issued by King Rājyaprakāśa of Kathmandu is not related to this temple. It records that only the king has the right to cut trees in the Kirtipur forts and if someone violates this regulation, he shall be fined twelve rupees.

historical_events.event_name: Construction of a Stone Pillar and Beam
historical_events.event_description: Jahara Siṃ Mānandhara constructed a stone pillar and beam to mount a bell.

Amoharamālā(jewellery made with coins) was offered to Bāghabhairava by a family living in Kirtipur. The family members, whose names can be deciphered from the readable part of the inscription, are: Tiyogī, Lumayi, Helamayi, Yogā, Mālasiṃha and Harṣavī.
Jahara Siṃ Mānandhara offered the bell which is installed in front of the temple.

historical_events.event_name: Offering of a Gilt Window and a Flag
historical_events.event_description: Karavani Kotavāla offered a gilt window and a flag to Bāghabhairava.

historical_events.event_name: Installation of a Gilt Pinnacle and a Flag
historical_events.event_description: During the reign of Purandarasiṃha, a certain Kvāthanāyaka (an officer of a fort) offered a gilt pinnacle and a flag to the temple.
A donation box (made of iron) was installed to collect cash donations. The box was offered by Mathurāma Maharjana.

historical_events.event_name: Adornment of the Main Entrance and the Toraṇa
historical_events.event_description: The main entrance of the temple and thetoraṇacrowning it were wrapped in brass plate by Bramhavatī Śreṣṭha and Tulavī Śreṣṭha.
Tavodhika Bhāro and his wife Lakṣmīśvarī offered a bell to Bāghabhairava.

historical_events.event_name: Land Grant by King Viṣṇu Malla and Establishment of Regulations
historical_events.event_description: The inscription is hard to decipher. The last numerical figure of the date is not clearly readable. It appears to be number 2.The legible part of the inscription records the land grant by King Viṣṇu Malla to organize the annual worship (which takes place on the first solar day of Bhādrā, also calledsiṃhasaṃkrānti). It also records various regulations regarding the organization of the annual worship.

historical_events.event_name: Visit of the President of Republic Nepal
historical_events.event_description: The first president of the Federal Democratic Republic of Nepal, Rāmavaraṇa Yādava, visited this temple and worshipped Bāghabhairava.
Gaṃgārāma and other Bhāros jointly offered a woodentoraṇa, crowning the Hiphaḥdyaḥ shrine (see object number KIR0004-005).
This is the earliest historical record related to this temple. The legible part of the inscription records a certain renovation of the temple carried out by Jagatapāla Varmā, a Mahāpātra of Pātan.
Kvāthanāyaka Viśvanātha Bhāro, probably an officer of a fort, offered a gilttoraṇa,khāpā(door),windowandguṃgvāka(?) to the Bāghabhairava Mandira.
Kvāthanāyaka Viśvanātha Bhāro offered something to Bāghavairava. Since the part of the inscription where this event is recorded is hard to decipher, what he actually offered remains unknown.

Māhilā from Samala Ṭola, Janakalāla from Kvācva Ṭola, Dhanabahādura from Lāykū Ṭola, Bhuyū from Thambāhāḥ Ṭola, and Herālāla from Kutujhvaḥ Ṭola jointly offered a brassṭoranawhich crowns the main entrance of the temple.
Satajīva Jñānī, her son Kāku, and other family members jointly offered a pair of brass flags which are flank the main entrance of the temple.
Two flags, flanking the main entrance of the temple, were restored by Lāla and his wife Māna Kumārī.
A group of Bhāvo community from Thaṃbāhāḥ Ṭola, Kirtipur offered the bell which is also installed in front of the temple.
